title: Logarithmic-space membership of the encoded languages
statement: Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input alphabet. Each of the five languages in the family associated with $N$—encoding input bits, input lengths, initial configurations, accepting configurations, and single computation steps—is decidable by a deterministic Turing machine using at most a constant multiple of $ loor{\log_2 n}+1$ space on inputs of length $n$.
